author: WP12
summary: A short new chapter on the build-time pipeline's module boundary, importer/processor/writer roles, source families, stable types, output-format-specific effect routes and the scope of the XNA compatibility claim. It is current at TARGET, and the site's Content Pipeline guide and pipeline internals already cover it in more depth; only the statement that XNB sources are transcoded, never wrapped, gained a new home (the transcoding boundaries section of the XNB type-readers deep dive).

concepts.text: modules/content-pipeline is a physical build-time module and not the runtime ContentManager; games link the content module and consume the results, tools link the pipeline module.
The pipeline imports authoring formats into typed intermediate values, runs processors, selects a writer and publishes CNB or XNB plus explicitly owned deployment files.
tokens: ResolveWriter(processed type, explicit writer, CNB or XNB)

concepts.text: An importer owns source parsing and source dependencies, a processor owns semantic conversion and parameters, and a writer owns the serialized artifact and its stable runtime type identity.
The pipeline context records dependencies, generated outputs, diagnostics and logical names so an importer cannot publish files behind the build engine's back.
CNA's generated parity report counts 128/128 XNA Content Pipeline types, 705/705 members and 27/27 enum values as represented, which is API representation, not automatic behaviour.
Behavioural closure is recorded separately across ten importers, eighteen source extensions, twelve processors and their parameter and default tests.
Built-in importers cover texture images, audio and media, fonts, models and glTF, effects, XNA intermediate XML and existing XNB where a compatibility route exists.
Processing includes texture conversion, font glyph and atlas work, audio handling, model, material and animation construction and effect compilation.
The writer is chosen from the processed type and the requested container, not merely from the source extension.
tokens: chooses a writer by the tuple (output format, processed stable type), not by file name

concepts.text: XNB is accepted as a source for supported built-in roots and transcoded to native CNB, and is also an output when a writer can express a genuine XNA artifact; arbitrary XNB bytes are never wrapped inside CNB.
tokens: It never wraps XNB bytes inside a CNB file
an .xnb is not written back as .xnb from this route

concepts.text: Pipeline values use explicit stable type strings rather than RTTI names in manifests or bytes; std::type_index is only an in-process check.
External references distinguish a runtime logical reference from a build dependency.
tokens: runtime references kept apart from build inputs

concepts.text: Custom C++ components register importers, processors, parameter metadata, writers and optional CNB codecs; the custom component API is experimental even though CNB container 1.0 and existing built-in schema ids are frozen.

Effect routes are output-format specific: Effect Framework bytecode is meaningful in XNB and on renderer paths that implement it, and CNB deliberately has no built-in Effect schema carrying one renderer API's bytecode.
Models converge through a shared intermediate and builder so glTF, CNJ, XNB and CNB do not invent separate runtime semantics.
tokens: The runtime and the build-time pipeline meet in the bytes on disk

concepts.text: Fonts produce atlas and glyph metrics; Song and Video writers publish a metadata CNB plus a byte-identical external media deployment file.
tokens: The media file itself is copied byte for byte beside the output as a deployment file

concepts.text: CNA's final pipeline audit closes the documented XNA surface and its chosen behavioural matrix (MSBuild content projects, custom extensions, measured defaults) but claims no binary identity with every XNA toolchain, third-party processor or managed plug-in execution; compatibility is strongest for named built-ins and fixtures.
tokens: Build behaviour is only as verified as the routes you actually use
